exposure: type of nursing support (on-site nurse vs. on-call nurse)
mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean section)
outcome: exclusive breastfeeding rate at 30 days of life
exclusive breastfeeding rate at 90 days of life
cohort: The study included 564 mother-baby dyads admitted between January 3 and March 31, 2018, from two Neonatology Units in the South of Italy.
finding: The study suggests that the presence of an on-site nurse during rooming-in encourages exclusive breastfeeding until three months of life, particularly for mothers who underwent caesarean section, although the overall exclusive breastfeeding rate at 90 days was 76.4% regardless of nursing support modality.
mod_finding: Infants born via cesarean section in the on-site nurse group demonstrated higher rates of exclusive breastfeeding at 30 and 90 days of life compared to the on-call group.
